comparison: Perfect alignment (Jaccard=1.0) on HI-FISH methodology claims (C4, C26-C37). Both evaluations find the method demonstration convincing and well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes specific technical details like low background in controls, while peer reviewers praise overall efficiency and potential to establish a new field standard.

Perfect alignment (Jaccard=1.0) on validation experiments and habituation protocol (C38-C44). Both evaluations support these methodological findings. OpenEval provides detailed analysis of controls and Hr38 induction data, while peer reviewers implicitly accept these as part of the convincing method demonstration without specific critique.

Strong alignment (Jaccard=0.789) on background context and technical limitations (C1-C3, C10-C17, C21-C25, C98-C103). Both evaluations support these claims. OpenEval validates literature citations and internal consistency, while peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge the technical constraints in Drosophila that this work addresses.

Strong alignment (Jaccard=0.762) on opto-HI-FISH circuit mapping (C7, C70-C80, C114-C117). Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval emphasizes validation through calcium imaging and convergence with independent studies, while peer reviewers highlight the method's versatility and potential for widespread use in circuit mapping.

Strong alignment (Jaccard=0.682) on HI-catFISH sequential behavior experiments (C8, C84-C97, C125-C126, C130-C131). Both evaluations support the findings about distinct P1a subpopulations. OpenEval notes appropriate caveats about interpretation, while peer reviewers emphasize this as compelling evidence for neuronal function in both aggression and courtship.

Strong alignment (Jaccard=0.643) on sensory integration findings (C59-C66, C108-C111). Both evaluations support conclusions about volatile and non-volatile cue requirements. OpenEval provides detailed statistical analysis and notes appropriate caveats, while peer reviewers accept these as part of compelling behavioral evidence without specific concerns.

Strong alignment (Jaccard=0.571) on differential activation patterns in P1a, aSP2, and TkFruM neurons (C45-C56, C106-C107). Both evaluations support these behavioral activation findings. OpenEval emphasizes consistency with prior functional studies and statistical significance, while peer reviewers treat these as convincing demonstrations of method utility.

Strong alignment (Jaccard=0.571) on comparison to Takayanagi-Kiya method (C135-C138). Both evaluations support the technical comparison and claims about temporal resolution advantages. OpenEval finds the comparison fair and appropriately speculative about combining methods, while peer reviewers implicitly accept by not raising concerns.

Partial alignment (Jaccard=0.25) on broader utility claims (C143-C144). Both evaluations support the method's potential for widespread application. OpenEval addresses future directions and VMHvl analogy (C139-C142), while peer reviewers focus specifically on versatility and potential to establish a new field standard.

Partial alignment (Jaccard=0.167) on P1a background literature (C118-C119). Both evaluations support these citations. OpenEval covers broader P1a context (C112-C113, C120-C129) including speculative mechanisms and apparent discrepancies, while peer reviewers focus on inherent limitations of IEG approaches when many neurons are present.

OpenEval evaluated background claims about IEG use in mammals vs Drosophila (C18-C20, C22-C23, C25, C101-C102), finding them well-supported by citations. No corresponding focused peer review evaluation found, though peer R10 touches on related context (C22, C25).
